pr.title: Move the Objective-C runtime helpers out of the clipboard module
pr.head: 36ea3252f84962548d4aa482cf2ee0e89b399c7d

summary: multipass copies a secret to the macOS clipboard with --clip. To do that it talks to AppKit, Apple's user-interface framework, through the Objective-C runtime: it looks up classes such as NSPasteboard, sends them messages through objc_msgSend, and loads AppKit with dlopen only when --clip runs, so no other command has AppKit in its process. At the base, all of that lives inside src/clipboard.rs, the program's only unsafe code.

The session-unlock plan adds a background agent that asks for Touch ID through LocalAuthentication, another Apple framework reached the same way. So this pull request moves the runtime helpers into a new module, src/objc.rs, that the clipboard and the coming Touch ID module can share. It is meant as a pure move: the clipboard's behaviour, its error messages, and when AppKit loads stay exactly as they were.
This is the bottom layer of the session-unlock work. It sits on the vault-key layers (#34 and below), and the layer above it (#37) builds the agent itself, adding src/touch_id.rs and src/sys.rs.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• objc_msgSend: the Objective-C runtime function that sends a message (calls a method). It must be called through a function pointer of the method's exact type, because on Apple silicon a variadic call puts arguments in different registers than the method reads.
  • send, send1, send2, send3: typed wrappers over objc_msgSend for methods with zero to three arguments.
  • Id: a raw pointer to an Objective-C object.
  • Autorelease pool: a runtime scope that frees the objects a framework hands back for the caller to drop. with_pool runs a closure inside one.
  • dlopen: the system call that loads a library into the running process.

cards.html:

  • Both suggestions are taken: load is an unsafe fn that requires a system framework, and Sel is private.
  • Two later merges of vault-key-move, the second bringing in the installer and upgrade work, resolved no conflict and left this pull request's diff unchanged. The head is clean: the moved code matches the base, AppKit still loads only for --clip, and every check passes.

groups.title: The shared Objective-C helpers
groups.kicker: A new module holds the runtime calls the clipboard defined for itself
intro: src/objc.rs declares the runtime functions multipass calls, from libSystem and from libobjc, and wraps them in a few helpers: load loads a framework by path, send through send3 send typed messages, class looks up a class by name, new_string and release make and free an NSString, and with_pool runs code inside an autorelease pool.

Every helper body except load is the clipboard's code moved unchanged. load is the clipboard's AppKit loader with the path and the name used in its error message turned into arguments. src/main.rs compiles the module only on macOS, as the clipboard's own macOS code already is.

The module is the unsafe layer, not a safe interface. send through send3, new_string, release, and load are unsafe fns whose callers must guarantee what the module doc names. class and with_pool are safe. Callers such as the clipboard wrap the unsafe helpers in safe interfaces.

checks.text: The bodies of send, send1, send2, send3, new_string, release, class, and with_pool match the base line for line, apart from pub and new comments, checked against the lines this pull request removes from src/clipboard.rs.

files.note: The new module. Compare each helper with the lines removed from src/clipboard.rs, and read the module doc against which functions are actually unsafe.

checks.text: The module doc matches the code: the functions it calls unsafe are exactly the pub unsafe fns in the file, and class and with_pool, which it calls safe, are plain pub fns.

load passes its path to dlopen, which runs that library's initializers, so it is unsafe and its # Safety section requires a system framework under /System/Library/Frameworks. Its one caller, the clipboard's load_appkit, passes AppKit's absolute path.
The error is could not load {what}: {reason}, and the clipboard passes AppKit for the clipboard, so the message is the same string as at the base. It names no value from the store.

groups.title: The clipboard as a caller
groups.kicker: The clipboard imports the helpers instead of defining them
intro: src/clipboard.rs keeps everything that is about the clipboard: the pasteboard constants, AppKit's absolute path, and the OnceLock that makes AppKit load at most once per process. It drops its own copies of the runtime declarations and helpers and imports them from crate::objc. Its Pasteboard methods are unchanged apart from spelling c_char as std::ffi::c_char.

files.note: Only the imports, the loader's body, and the module doc change. The loader now calls load in an unsafe block, with a comment that APPKIT is a system framework's absolute path. The private-pasteboard tests at the bottom are unchanged and still pass.

checks.text: AppKit still loads only when --clip needs the clipboard. Release builds of the base and this head each load 81 images for --help, --version, and upgrade --help, none of them AppKit, and tests/startup.rs still asserts that for --version.

The three clipboard::tests tests pass against a private pasteboard, so writing, concealing, and clearing still work through the moved helpers. cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test, and the cargo tree dependency check all pass on this head.

groups.title: The rule on Apple's frameworks
groups.kicker: AGENTS.md names both modules as the program's only unsafe code
intro: AGENTS.md holds the instructions agents follow in this repository. At the base, its rule that Apple's system frameworks count like the standard library says src/clipboard.rs holds the program's only unsafe code. The rule now says the clipboard's calls go through src/objc.rs, which holds the unsafe runtime helpers, and that src/clipboard.rs wraps them in a safe interface. Those two modules hold the only unsafe code. Any new unsafe code still goes in a module like them, behind a safe interface, with a comment on what each call needs of its arguments.

files.note: One sentence of the dependencies section changes.

checks.text: The sentence matches the code: src/objc.rs exports mostly unsafe fn helpers, and the clipboard's Pasteboard is the safe interface over them. The rule asks for nothing less than at the base. The base's src/upgrade.rs and installer add no unsafe code, so the two modules it names are still the only ones that hold any.
